item.title: Special Postage Stamp: Special postage stamp to be issued
item.description: Myanmar Post under the Ministry of Transport and Communications, will issue and sell a special 200-kyat postage stamp featuring Myanmar Coffee cultivation in honor of locally grown Coffee. The stamp will be available from 9:30 a.m. on Friday, March 27th, 2026. The special stamps will be sold simultaneously at the Nay Pyi Taw Central Post Office, Yangon General Post Office, Mandalay General Post Office, and major post offices across regions and states. item.title: Coordination Meeting: Preparations for Thingyan Festival discussed
item.description: Myanmar is making full preparations for the upcoming 2026 Thingyan Festival in April, aiming for greater public participation and a more lively and peaceful celebration. The second coordination meeting for the successful holding of the festival was held at the Taninthayi Region Government Office in Dawei on Tuesday. item.title: North Korean leader attends artistic performance in Pyongyang
item.description: North Korean President Kim Jong Un attended an artistic performance in Pyongyang. The show celebrated the outcome of the First Session of the 15th Supreme People’s Assembly, during which parliament re-elected Kim as president of state affairs. Kim watched a large-scale artistic performance featuring music, dance, and theatrical acts. The show highlighted national pride, revolutionary history, and cultural traditions of North Korea. item.title: Iran denies any negotiations with US
item.description: The U.S.-Israel-Iran conflict entered its 24th day on Monday, with attention focused on a sharp divergence between the United States and Iran over whether the two sides are engaged in talks. On Monday, U.S. President Donald Trump said he had ordered a five-day delay of planned strikes on Iranian power plants and energy facilities, citing what he described as “very good and productive conversations” over the past two days aimed at easing tensions in the Middle East. item.title: New Joint Operation Command chief
item.description: The new chief of Japan’s Self-Defense Forces (SDF) command, which oversees Ground, Maritime and Air Self-Defense Forces, has stressed the need for better coordination among the three branches amid growing global uncertainties. Admiral Tawara Tateki became the commander of the Joint Operations Command on Monday, replacing General Nagumo Ken-ichiro, who was the first head of the command launched last year. item.title: Turkmenistan celebrates Nowruz with great fanfare
item.description: Celebrations take place in the foothills of the Kopetdag Mountains. Dances in traditional costumes take place near snow-white yurts, meat is cooked over a fire, and carpets are sold in the palaces. National songs and poems dedicated to the holiday are recited. Participants also demonstrate their skills in ancient crafts, such as silk and carpet making, and the preparation of traditional delicacies. In the evening, a bonfire is lit in the Nowruz Valley. item.title: Cherry blossoms draw crowds as they approach full bloom in Tokyo
item.description: Tokyo's meteorologists declared the start of the much-loved cherry blossom season in the Japanese capital on Thursday, as residents prepare to host outdoor picnics under dazzling floral displays. The cherry season for Tokyo starts when the official sample tree at Yasukuni Shrine opens at least five flowers.
